notes: Functionally sound, including handling a root that names a link, but the zip Open past-end special-casing is hacky, squashfs NewObject retry logic is convoluted, there are no docs, and squashfs tests depend on mksquashfs.

Works for both backends, including a root naming the .rclonelink. NewObject has a two-step fallback lookup, and the zip Open special-cases EOF for symlinks in a somewhat clunky way. Tests are good, including copy and escape.
Production code is essentially identical to the reference and adds docs, but its tests are thin: zip has no seek/range checks, and squashfs is only exercised through mksquashfs, which may be skipped.

Source matches the reference exactly. Tests are thinner: the zip unit test only checks listing and a full read (no seek/range or suffix-less NewObject checks), and squashfs coverage depends on mksquashfs being installed.

Works for the main flows, but zip appends the suffix after root filtering and squashfs root detection has no suffix fallback, so a root naming `link.rclonelink` isn't recognised while the bare name is; it also adds an unrelated List ErrorDirNotFound change, and its tests are good.

Basic listing, reading and copying work. In both backends a root given as the suffixed name (e.g. archive.zip/src/link.txt.rclonelink) is not recognised as the symlink object, because zip adds the suffix after the root check and squashfs root detection uses raw names; this breaks agreement with listed names. It also includes an extra List ErrorDirNotFound change, and the tests use os.Chdir.

Handles name clashes and a root at a link with extensive tests, but it eagerly opens and reads every symlink member during readZip (costly over S3), silently drops links on read errors, and adds an unrelated List error-mapping change.

Handles name collisions and symlink roots. However, it eagerly opens and reads every zip symlink member during readZip, which is costly for remote archives and silently skips symlinks on read errors. It also adds an unrelated List-on-non-directory behaviour change.

Code matches the reference exactly, and the tests are comprehensive: unit tests for both backends with a squashfs fixture, seek/range, a regular .rclonelink member, end-to-end copy recreating the symlink, and the hostile-archive escape.

Source changes match the reference for both zip and squashfs. Tests are thorough: skip without --links, suffix naming, NewObject agreement, seek/range, a regular .rclonelink member, end-to-end copy to a symlink and the hostile escape case. It also adds docs and a small testdata image.

Correct for both backends and goes further than the reference by giving regular members priority on name clashes and supporting a root that names a link; the cost is a sizeable, harder-to-follow restructuring of readZip, though its tests are thorough (seek/range, collisions, root, hostile copy).

Correct, and goes beyond the reference with name-collision precedence and root-at-symlink handling. The cost is a sizeable refactor of readZip (zipEntryFor/addObject/removeLink, altered singleObject loop logic) plus extra squashfs lookup helpers, which makes the change heavier and riskier than needed.
